# Into One Grain of Salt

## From a Grain to Its Particles

To see what atoms do to each other, we have to look at them. Take one grain of salt, about half a millimetre wide, and imagine magnifying it a few million times (about 25 lakh times). The grain would then be more than a kilometre across, and each tiny particle in it would look about as big as the grain you started with.

<!-- STEP id="claim" -->
## What We Will Find

In the coming lessons we will find what an atom is built from, and what makes a sodium atom different from a chlorine atom. Then we will see what those two atoms do to each other to become salt, and that will explain the bulb.

<!-- STEP id="hook" -->
## One Question First

For a very long time nobody could see an atom, so before we go in we should ask why anyone believed in atoms at all.

**In the next lesson we will see how a simple balance gave the first real evidence.**
